record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: For every k >= 5, does there exist an infinite (k/(k-1))^+-free word over k letters with letter frequency 1/(k+1), and for every k >= 6, does there exist such a word with letter frequency 1/(k-1)?

evidence.quote: (stronger version of Dejean’s conjecture): – For every k>= 5, there is an infinite (k/k- 1)+-free word over k letters with letter frequency 1/k + 1. – For every k>= 6, there is an infinite (k/k- 1)+-free word over k-letter with letter frequency 1/k- 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_k = \{1, 2, \ldots, k\}$ be an alphabet of size $k$. For a real number $\alpha > 1$, an $\alpha^+$-free word is an infinite word over $\Sigma_k$ that contains no factor of the form $u^e$ with rational exponent $e > \alpha$ (where $u^e$ for $|u| = p$ and $e = n/p$ denotes a factor of length $n$ which is a prefix of $u^\omega$). The repetition threshold for $k$ letters is $k/(k-1)$ for $k \geq 5$ (Dejean's theorem). The frequency of a letter $a \in \Sigma_k$ in an infinite word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots$ is defined as
$$\mathrm{freq}_w(a) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{|\{i \leq n : w_i = a\}|}{n},$$
when the limit exists.

Prove or disprove the following two statements:

(i) For every integer $k \geq 5$, there exists an infinite $(k/(k-1))^+$-free word over $\Sigma_k$ in which some letter has frequency exactly $1/(k+1)$.

(ii) For every integer $k \geq 6$, there exists an infinite $(k/(k-1))^+$-free word over $\Sigma_k$ in which some letter has frequency exactly $1/(k-1)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: Chalopin and Ochem established the cases $k=5$ (frequency $1/6$) and $k=6$ (frequency $1/5$) of these stronger versions of Dejean's conjecture. Tunev and Shur proved related stronger versions of Dejean's conjecture for odd alphabet sizes $n = 7, 9, \ldots, 101$. The general conjecture for all $k \geq 5$ (resp. $k \geq 6$) does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Dejean's conjecture and letter frequency (Chalopin–Ochem)
status_evidence.snippet: There exist an infinite (5/4+)-free word over a 5 letter alphabet with letter frequency 1/6 and an infinite (6/5+)-free word over a 6 letter alphabet with letter frequency 1/5.
status_evidence.claim: Cases k=5 and k=6 of the stronger conjecture about letter frequency 1/(k+1) are settled.

status_evidence.title: On Two Stronger Versions of Dejean's Conjecture (Tunev–Shur)
status_evidence.snippet: For odd n = 7, 9, ..., 101, the authors proved the strongest possible result in this direction, providing affirmative answers to these stronger versions of Dejean's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Stronger versions of Dejean's conjecture have been proven for odd alphabet sizes 7 through 101, but not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: On Circular Threshold Words and Other Stronger Versions of Dejean's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes stronger versions of Dejean's conjecture by constructing threshold words with additional properties.
status_evidence.claim: Stronger versions of Dejean's conjecture continue to be actively investigated.
